CXC-WHAT.title: Composer Is a Visual Builder That Is Itself a Bus Application

properties.definition: A desktop tool that lets a builder assemble a ComposeUX control surface visually — drag widgets onto a canvas, group them into modules, bind them to bus namespaces — and emit a ComposeIO configuration as the output artifact.
properties.key-insight: Composer dogfoods the platform it designs for. Its own panels (palette, canvas, property editor, preview, inspectors) are autonomous modules communicating over an internal ComposeIO bus. No panel holds a direct reference to another. The same namespace pub/sub that wires a physical button to a relay wires Composer's own UI together.
properties.role: Move the specificity boundary for ComposeUX from code to visual layout — a builder should never need to write Python to produce a working control surface.

CXC-CREDO.title: An Intelligence Drives Composer Identically to a Human

properties.definition: Every builder action is a bus message. A human dragging a widget and an Intelligence publishing `composer/canvas/widget_added` are peers — the bus is the equalizing layer, and neither path is privileged.
properties.key-insight: This is the design credo, not a feature bolted on. Because the interaction surface is the bus, Composer is drivable headlessly, fully observable, and scriptable. The capability is inherited by the surfaces it builds: a widget authored in Composer is itself bus-native and equally Intelligence-drivable.
properties.implication: The MCP bridge ([CXC-FEAT-INTEL]) is a client of the same bus a human uses — it adds no privileged back door.

CXC-HIER.title: The Design Hierarchy Is Design > Module > Widget

properties.definition: A Composer design describes a complete ComposeUX surface: modules arranged in a spatial grid, each module containing widgets, with namespace bindings between them. The hierarchy is explicit and mirrors real ComposeIO systems (modules are boards; boards carry buttons/relays/gauges).
properties.constraint: Module boundaries are visible on the canvas and are also namespace boundaries. Cross-module bindings use global scope; intra-module bindings use local scope.

properties.role: The spatial editing surface. Add/move/resize/remove modules and widgets on a grid; module frames are distinct visual groups.

Presents available widget types; publishing a selection begins placement. The catalog is a discoverable registry, not a hardcoded list — custom widget types register without modifying Composer source.
properties.built-in-widgets: ButtonWidget, GaugeWidget, RelayWidget, CoordinateEntryWidget, BusMonitorWidget, TabWidget
properties.gap: No ImageWidget or Callout/annotation widget yet — blocks the M31 flagship testbed. Tracked in the widgets subcategory.

properties.role: Configure a selected widget's properties and its namespace bindings visually — pickers and drag-connect, never typing raw namespace strings. State-engine selection is a picker (binary, tri_level, stop_light, continuous_0_255, enum, json).
Instantiates actual ComposeUX widgets on a real ComposeIO bus, separate from the internal tool bus. Clicking a preview button publishes state; bound widgets respond. Not a mockup — a running system.

Composer runs an in-process internal bus (tool messages: `composer/selection`, `composer/canvas/*`) and an external bus bridged over MQTT (Intelligence protocol, remote drive). The external bridge auto-connects when `COMPOSEUX_MQTT_BROKER` is set.

An MCP server speaks the `composer/intelligence/*` protocol over the MQTT broker — exports intent/request_state/request_layout, imports state/layout snapshots — letting an Intelligence drive and observe a live Composer GUI as a bus peer.

Save, load, and export designs to ComposeIO config. Disk I/O is a bus request handled by a non-visual FileOpsModule; visual modules rebuild from the shared design document on `composer/file/loaded`. Round-trip fidelity (byte-identical save→load→save) is the standing goal.

Slices R1–R5 (C3-first), CH32 deferred.

properties.role: The foundational Composer specification set — principles, architecture, internal bus, module contracts, serialization, preview, intelligence API, widget renderers, and more. Fully converted from SMD to FactLattice `.lts` in the migration test-case pass.
properties.conventions: 99-composeio-conventions.smd (symlink into the ComposeIO platform corpus, which remains SMD until its own migration); domain profile `platform-composeio.lts` registers the CXC- prefix.

CXC-DD-LATTICE.title: Adopt FactLattice; Full SMD→LTS Conversion as Migration Test Case

properties.decision: Composer specifications are authored in FactLattice `.lts`. The full 16-document SMD corpus was converted to `.lts` in a single scripted pass — deliberately, to exercise and validate the SMD→FactLattice migration workflow on a real project. ComposeIO is the first project migrated end-to-end.
properties.rationale: Making the migration workflow itself the deliverable produces a reusable, verified recipe (rename + `domain:` binding + surgical intra-corpus ref rewrite; cross-corpus refs preserved) and a uniform corpus that is easier to tool and reason about than a mixed one.
properties.change: "Composer spec corpus fully converted from SMD (.smd) to FactLattice (.lts) in a single migration pass; supersedes the earlier opportunistic-migration plan."
context_for_change: prior_state: "16 Composer specs in SMD; an earlier revision of this decision chose opportunistic per-area migration to avoid up-front effort."
reasoning: "David elected to use ComposeIO as the test case for a full SMD→LTS conversion. Doing the whole corpus now yields a proven, reusable migration recipe and removes the coexistence boundary."
rejected_alternative: "Opportunistic migration (convert each .smd only when its area is revised) — the prior decision, now superseded."
counter_argument: "Full migration touches documents not otherwise being worked, risking churn."

counter_response: "The migration is mechanical and script-driven (rename + domain + ref-rewrite, no content rewrite), so churn is bounded and verifiable; VERIFY steps confirmed 78 intra-corpus refs rewritten and all cross-corpus refs preserved."

invalidating_assumption: "That the conversion is purely mechanical. If future enrichment (multi-notation, confidence annotations) requires per-document human-in-the-loop rewriting, treat that as separate work, not migration."
implication: "The corpus is uniformly .lts; `tools/smd_to_lts.py` is the reusable recipe for the next corpus (e.g. the ComposeIO platform spec/ set)."

DP-CXC-1.title: The Composer Is a ComposeIO Application

implication: The Composer's internal architecture validates ComposeIO's design principles. If ComposeIO cannot build a complex desktop tool, the platform has expressiveness gaps that need fixing.

The internal bus uses the same `ComposeIOBus` class, the same message types, the same namespace semantics as any ComposeIO application. The only difference is scope — all namespaces are local (in-process).
Each Composer module can be developed and tested in isolation. A palette module with a mock bus is a valid test fixture. A canvas module driven by scripted bus messages is a valid integration test.
properties.test: If any Composer module imports another module's class or calls another module's method directly, the design has failed. All communication flows through the bus.
properties.learned-from: Formation Studio's tight coupling between `ComponentPane`, `Designer`, and `StylePane` — each holds direct references to the others, making testing and modification difficult.

DP-CXC-2.title: Visual Layout Is the Primary Artifact

implication: Every layout property expressible in ComposeIO config (grid position, column weight, padding, sizing) must be manipulable visually on the canvas. If a layout property requires YAML editing, the Composer's canvas is incomplete.
The generated YAML is always valid against [SPEC:CIO-CONFIG-SCHEMA]. The Composer does not produce intermediate formats that require post-processing.
Visual layout and YAML config are kept in sync bidirectionally. Editing the YAML externally and reloading it in the Composer must produce the correct visual state.
properties.test: If a builder needs to open a text editor to achieve a layout that the Composer's canvas supports conceptually, the design has failed.
properties.contrast-with: Formation Studio, which produces tkinter-specific XML that cannot be used outside the Formation ecosystem.

DP-CXC-3.title: Namespace Binding Is Visual, Not Textual

implication: The binding editor provides a visual representation of namespace connections: source widgets, transform chains, and target widgets. Compound bindings with conditions are expressed as visual rule cards, not raw YAML.

The namespace registry for the design-in-progress is a first-class, always-visible artifact. The builder sees all registered namespaces, their state engines, current publishers, and current subscribers at a glance.
State engine selection is a dropdown or picker, not a text field. The builder selects `binary`, `tri_level`, `stop_light`, `continuous_0_255`, or defines a custom `enum` with values — all visually.
properties.test: If creating a simple button-to-relay binding requires typing a namespace string, the design has failed. The builder should be able to drag from a button to a relay (or select from a namespace list) to create the binding.

implication: The preview bus is a separate `ComposeIOBus` instance from the Composer's internal bus. The Composer's internal bus carries tool messages (`composer/selection`, `composer/layout`). The preview bus carries the user's design messages (`ftl_arm`, `sublight_engines`).
Preview updates on every canvas change. Adding a widget, moving it, changing a binding — the preview rebuilds automatically. The feedback loop is visual and immediate.
Dual-renderer preview is supported: CTk (desktop approximation) and LVGL (pixel-accurate embedded preview via `LVGLCanvas`). The builder sees both side-by-side when designing for embedded targets.
properties.test: If a binding that works in the preview produces different behavior when deployed to a real ComposeIO runtime, the preview is broken.
properties.see-also: [DP-CIO-4] for state engine semantics that the preview must faithfully reproduce.

implication: The palette module only knows how to display available widgets and publish selection events. It does not know about the canvas, the property editor, or the preview. It publishes to `composer/palette/selected` and its job is done.
Module boundaries are namespace boundaries. To understand what a module does, read its namespace subscriptions and publications. The bus namespace registry is the Composer's architecture diagram.

Modules can be added, removed, or replaced without modifying other modules. A builder who wants a custom property editor for a specific widget type adds a module that subscribes to `composer/selection` and publishes to `composer/config` — the existing property editor continues to work alongside it.
The Composer's own layout (which panels are where, their sizes, their visibility) is itself a ComposeIO config. The Composer is bootstrapped from its own output format.
properties.test: If removing the binding editor module causes the canvas or palette to malfunction, module boundaries are violated.
properties.learned-from: Formation Studio's `StudioFeature` base class attempted this separation but enforced it weakly — features accessed the main studio object and each other directly.

implication: The Composer canvas supports nested composition. A module frame contains widget slots. A design contains module frames arranged in a grid. This mirrors how ComposeIO systems actually work: modules are physical boards containing buttons/relays/gauges, and the system is a collection of modules.
Module boundaries are visible on the canvas. A `ButtonPanelWidget` module is a distinct visual group, not a flat collection of buttons mixed with other widgets.
Bindings between modules are visually distinct from bindings within a module. Cross-module bindings use global scope; intra-module bindings use local scope. The Composer enforces this automatically.
properties.test: If a builder cannot tell which module owns which widget by looking at the canvas, the visual hierarchy is inadequate.

implication: The internal representation preserves source ordering, comments (where supported), and whitespace conventions. The Composer is a faithful editor, not an opinionated formatter.

YAML generated by the Composer is human-readable. Property keys appear in a consistent, logical order. Indentation is standard. The output is something a builder would be comfortable reading and could hand-edit if needed.

Loading YAML that was hand-edited outside the Composer must work correctly. The Composer is not the only way to create ComposeIO configs — it is the visual way. Hand-authored YAML and Composer-generated YAML are interchangeable.
properties.test: `diff original.yaml <(compose-composer load original.yaml | compose-composer save -)` must produce no output for any valid ComposeIO config.

implication: The palette discovers widgets from a registry. Built-in widgets (ButtonWidget, RelayWidget, GaugeWidget, CoordinateEntryWidget, BusMonitorWidget) ship with the Composer. Custom widgets are registered via a plugin directory or config entry.

Each registered widget type declares its configurable properties, its namespace requirements (how many namespaces it consumes/produces), and its visual preview behavior. This metadata drives the property editor and binding editor automatically.

OtherWidgets (`other_widgets`) is a first-class plugin. All OtherProject widgets — OtherProjectWidget, OtherProjectAsyncWidget, SliderWithLabel, MetricsCardWidget, etc. — are registerable in the palette without modifying Composer source.
properties.test: If registering a new widget type requires modifying any Composer source file, the extension mechanism is broken.
properties.see-also: [DP-CIO-1] — same principle applied to UX widgets instead of hardware modules.

implication: Commands are published to the bus as events on `composer/history`. The undo system is itself a bus module — it subscribes to command events, maintains the stack, and publishes undo/redo actions back to the bus.

Each command captures the minimum state needed for reversal. A move command stores old and new positions. A property change stores old and new values. A binding change stores the old and new binding configs.
Undo is available during live preview. If the builder changes a binding and the preview shows wrong behavior, undo reverts both the canvas and the preview.
properties.test: Any sequence of N operations followed by N undos must restore the design to its original state.

implication: Every user action is a bus message. An Intelligence watching `composer/canvas/widget_added`, `composer/binding/created`, and `composer/config/changed` has a complete, structured event stream of the builder's design session.

The Composer can be driven headlessly via bus messages. An Intelligence that publishes to `composer/canvas/add_widget` and `composer/binding/create` can generate UX layouts programmatically. The visual canvas is a view of the bus state, not the source of truth.
Layout reporting from `other_widgets` (`report_layout()`, `report_layout_flat()`) works on the Composer's own UI and on the preview, giving Intelligences pixel-accurate spatial understanding.
properties.see-also: OtherProjectWidget's EventBus integration for interaction tracing and simulated input.

properties.role: Carries all editor-level communication between Composer modules (palette, canvas, property editor, binding editor, history, bus inspector).
properties.scope: Local only. Never leaves the Composer process.
properties.namespace-prefix: `composer/` — all internal namespaces live under this prefix.
properties.lifetime: Created at Composer startup. Destroyed at shutdown.

properties.role: The real ComposeIO bus that designed widgets connect to. This is the same bus that physical hardware, MQTT brokers, CAN networks, and service hubs participate in.
properties.scope: Local, global, or remote — depending on available transports.
properties.transport: Any combination — in-process for offline design, MQTT/CAN/UART for live hardware.
properties.namespace-prefix: None — these are the user's real application namespaces (`ftl_arm`, `sublight_engines`, etc.).
properties.lifetime: Connected/disconnected independently of Composer lifecycle. The Composer functions in offline mode (in-process-only design bus) when no external bus is available.

properties.connection-lifecycle: The builder connects/disconnects the design bus at runtime via a connection panel. Connecting adds transports. Disconnecting removes them. The design bus always exists (at minimum as in-process) — transport connections are additive.
properties.auto-discovery: When a transport connects, the design bus receives `discovery` messages from existing modules. The Composer's namespace registry updates to show hardware-reported namespaces alongside designer-defined ones.
properties.conflict-detection: If a hardware module publishes to a namespace the builder has defined in their design, the Composer flags the conflict (duplicate publisher). The builder resolves by renaming, merging, or accepting shared publication.

properties.hot-swap: Modules can be added/removed at runtime. Adding a module subscribes it to relevant namespaces. Removing a module unsubscribes and destroys the frame. Other modules are unaffected (they never held a reference).
properties.module-config: Each module's initial state (position, size, visibility, collapsed/expanded) is itself a ComposeIO config loaded at startup. The Composer bootstraps from its own output format.

properties.rebuild-trigger: Preview rebuilds when any `composer/canvas/*`, `composer/config/*`, or `composer/binding/*` message is received on the internal bus.
properties.rebuild-strategy: Incremental when possible (property change updates one widget). Full rebuild on structural changes (widget added/removed, binding changed).
properties.bus-continuity: The design bus is NOT restarted on preview rebuild. State is preserved. A gauge that was at 75% stays at 75% after a layout change.

properties.authority: The design document is modified ONLY through bus commands. No module mutates it directly. The history module captures every mutation for undo/redo.
properties.persistence: The design document serializes to ComposeIO YAML (see 04-composer-serialization.lts). The in-memory representation and the YAML are isomorphic.

properties.single-select: Default. Clicking a widget selects it and deselects all others.
properties.multi-select: Shift+click or drag-select. Multiple widgets selected. Property editor shows common properties.
properties.module-select: Clicking a module header selects the module. Property editor shows module-level config.

properties.design-file: `.compose.yaml` — the Composer's native format. Contains layout + config + bindings in a single document.
properties.export-files: Standard `.yaml` ComposeIO config files — one per module, plus a system-level bindings file. These are deployment artifacts.

properties.rationale: PyYAML does not preserve comments, key ordering, or quoting style. `ruamel.yaml` in round-trip mode preserves all formatting.
properties.fallback: If `ruamel.yaml` is unavailable, fall back to PyYAML with a warning that round-trip fidelity is degraded.

properties.limitation: Imported designs will have auto-arranged layout. The builder's first action is typically rearranging the visual layout.
properties.multi-file: Importing multiple ComposeIO YAML files creates one module per file, all placed in the same design.

implication: If a compound binding works in the preview, it will work in deployment. If it breaks in the preview, it would break in deployment.
Hardware modules connected to the design bus participate in the preview. A physical button press updates the preview's relay widget. A preview slider changes a physical gauge.
properties.contrast-with: Formation Studio's preview which renders static tkinter widgets without behavior.

properties.surfaces: Module frames use `theme.SURFACE_ELEVATED`. Preview container uses `theme.SURFACE_PRIMARY`.
properties.override: Builder can select theme variant in preview toolbar. Theme changes do not affect the design — they affect preview rendering only.

properties.divergence-detection: If the CTk and LVGL renderers show different visual states for the same namespace value, the preview flags a rendering divergence. This catches cases where the LVGL styling or layout does not match the CTk behavior.

properties.timing: Full rebuild completes in <200ms for designs with up to 50 widgets. Above that, rebuild shows a brief loading indicator.

implication: Every action achievable by clicking the canvas is achievable by publishing a bus message. There is no "visual-only" capability. The Intelligence API is not an adapter or wrapper — it is the same namespace registry that modules use.
An Intelligence can design a complete UX headlessly (no Composer window). The `.compose.yaml` is generated from bus state, not from canvas state. The canvas renders bus state — it does not own it.
Human and Intelligence can co-edit simultaneously. Both publish to the same namespaces. The History module records all commands regardless of source. Undo works uniformly.

use-case: CI/CD pipelines generating UX configs from specifications.
Intelligence generating designs in batch without GUI overhead.
Testing — validate that a sequence of bus commands produces the expected `.compose.yaml`.

implication: Agents work in parallel on isolated worktrees. No merge conflicts because no shared files (except the base class and bus, which are written first by the skeleton agent).
Integration testing is bus-driven. A test publishes messages and asserts responses. No mock objects, no module cross-references.
An agent can be re-run to improve its module without affecting other modules.
properties.analogy: This is [DP-CIO-2] applied to development. Agents are connected by shared namespace, not by shared code.

CXC-FLAUTH.title: Composer Flow Mode — Headless Widget Authoring

CXC-FLAUTH-INTENT.title: Author Logic Where You Author Displays

properties.definition: extend Flow mode ([SPEC:CXC-FLOW]) so a declarative headless widget ([SPEC:CXC-HEADLESS]) is created, wired, expression-authored, scheduled, and deployed as a **logic node** in the same node-graph as visual widgets and namespace hubs. The graph remains a *synced projection* of the `.compose.yaml` — edit in Flow / Bindings / Source, all stay in lockstep; Flow is not a new authority.
properties.closes: [CXC-HW-AUTHORING] (Flow mode is the headless editor) using the [CXC-FL-HEADLESS] forward hook.

CXC-FLAUTH-NODE.title: A Headless Widget Rendered as a Node

properties.model: a `FlowNode.kind="logic"` (hook already structural) drawn with a **λ** badge: **input ports** (left) = subscribed namespaces, **output ports** (right) = published namespaces, a **schedule badge** (∞ continuous / ⏱ periodic / ⚡ bus-triggered), and an expr/purpose summary. Title = widget id.

properties.definition: a machine-readable table of a headless widget's ports + schedule, from its `.compose.yaml` (subscribed namespaces = inputs; `outputs:`/publish namespaces = outputs; the `headless.schedule` block = mode + interval/trigger). Mirrors the [CXC-BE-INTROSPECT] pattern (behavior/attr introspection) so `build_graph` and the inspector render from tables, not hardcoding.

generalize publish-wire authoring beyond Button-class — a drag from a logic node's output port to a namespace hub writes the widget's publish/`outputs:` entry into the `.compose.yaml`; the hub gains a publisher. Round-trips byte-identically; Bindings/Source reflect it.

properties.create: a **＋ Logic node** affordance adds a new headless widget (named, empty ports, a default `continuous` schedule) to the design.

properties.surface: selecting a logic node switches the WC to the **Flow inspector** (already lens-following, [CXC-FL-SCALE]); it shows each output's `expr` in an inline editor, **live-validated by the DSL parser** ([SPEC:CXC-DSL] `dsl.try_parse`) — a green valid / red error state as you type. The **Source tab** remains the always-available raw escape hatch (the expr is just YAML).
properties.decision: expr is authored inline in the inspector per output, NOT a separate editor — the inspector is where the selected node is authored. Reuses the [SPEC:CXC-BINDEDIT] editor idioms.
properties.boundary: only the sanctioned `expr:` sites ([CXC-DSL-SITES]); arbitrary code stays refused ([CXC-BIND-BOUNDARY]).

properties.surface: a three-mode picker in the inspector — **continuous** (10 Hz daemon) / **periodic** (interval, editable) / **bus-triggered** (trigger namespace/pattern). Writes the widget's `headless.schedule` block ([CXC-HW-SCHEDULE]); the **schedule travels in the widget** ([CXC-HW-DEPLOY]), the roster stays pure membership.

a **deploy card** — assign logic node(s) to a `runtime_id`; the card shows the roster path `bus://assets/headless/<runtime_id>.roster.yaml` and members; a **Push** action writes the roster + each widget config to bus_storage via the **Pass-1 loader** ([CXC-HW-DEPLOY], `BusStorageLoader` — no new deploy plumbing).

CXC-FLAUTH-CONFIRM.title: See It Run (the confirmation half of [CXC-HW-INTROSPECT])

properties.decision: the **Confirmation** half of observability lands here because its data is already reachable and it couples to surfaces built anyway; **Diagnosis** (tick trace / internal state) is Pass 4 ([CXC-HW-INTROSPECT]).

CXC-BE-INTENT.status: operational (2026-07-07) — C1–C8 all PASS (19 compliance tests in `tests/render/test_bindedit.py`; suite 251 green macOS, 247+4skip RPi5); Intelligence-over-MQTT smoke 8/8 from BOTH platforms (`tests/render/smoke_bindedit_intelligence_mqtt.py`); new-chrome screenshots pixel-compared macOS↔RPi5 (7 full-window shots: 28 px total, all Δ≤1; the pop-out shot 0-px identical).

properties.definition: After M4, a builder can place/arrange/preview widgets but must hand-edit YAML to bind namespaces or add behaviors — violating DP-CXC-3 ("namespace binding is visual, not textual"). This pass makes binding + behavior authoring visual, and adds a synced YAML view for transparency and power-editing.
properties.status: operational (2026-07-07) — C1–C8 all PASS (19 compliance tests in `tests/render/test_bindedit.py`; suite 251 green macOS, 247+4skip RPi5); Intelligence-over-MQTT smoke 8/8 from BOTH platforms (`tests/render/smoke_bindedit_intelligence_mqtt.py`); new-chrome screenshots pixel-compared macOS↔RPi5 (7 full-window shots: 28 px total, all Δ≤1; the pop-out shot 0-px identical).

CXC-BE-BINDING.title: Bind Attributes & Configure Behaviors Without Typing YAML

properties.role: In the WC, for the selected widget: bind any bindable attribute to a namespace, and attach state-driven behaviors — authoring the [SPEC:CXC-BIND] forms declaratively.
properties.placement: lives in the WC — Overview's bindings section becomes interactive, or a dedicated Bindings sub-panel; the selected-widget context drives it (same selection bus the other tabs use).
properties.test: bind `visible` to a namespace via the picker with zero YAML typed → the exported `.compose.yaml` carries the binding; configure a `blink` via the UI → the previewed widget blinks.
properties.implemented: `composer/bindpanel.py` (BindingsPanel — a dedicated WC **Bindings** tab; the WC is now 5 tabs Overview/Layers/Widgets/Bindings/Source, `composer/wc/active_tab` enum extended, Intelligence-switchable). Picker Save emits the SIMPLEST [SPEC:CXC-BIND] form (bare-string for visible/opacity/rotation/scale when no options, object form otherwise) via `composer/config/widget_changed` — every edit is a bus command ([DP-CXC-1]). Behavior form: trigger chips (is/is_exact/truthy/in/always) + namespace picker (declared-namespace chips or type-one, auto-declared on save) + behavior/target chips + schema-driven param fields. The WW preview now wires `attr_bindings` + `behaviors` to the design bus/host BehaviorEngine (stale instances removed per rebuild), so a configured blink runs live in the canvas; a **PREVIEW BUS — TEST STATES** section flips trigger namespaces (the same bit an Intelligence flips). Undo/redo (Cmd/Ctrl+Z · Shift+Z / Ctrl+Y + topbar buttons) covers all binding/behavior edits incl. raw-property restore.
properties.change: "Drag-connect is DEFERRED; the namespace picker is the shipped binding gesture."
context_for_change: prior_state: "The spec offered 'picker / drag-connect' as alternative gestures."

reasoning: "Drag-connect from a WW widget to a WC namespace row needs a cross-panel drag/ghost-wire mechanism the engine does not have — exactly the 'new bus/selection mechanism' the build order marks ESCALATE-don't-guess. The picker alone satisfies the C1 criterion (zero YAML typed)."
invalidating_assumption: "That the picker is ergonomically sufficient at fleet scale; if binding volume makes it slow, drag-connect returns as its own slug with an engine drag primitive."

properties.role: The editor enumerates what is bindable/configurable by reading declarative tables the engine exposes — it does not hardcode them.
properties.test: adding a new behavior to the engine + its param-schema row makes it appear in the editor with correct fields, no editor code change.
properties.implemented: `engine/bindings.py` — `UNIVERSAL_BINDABLE_ATTRS` (visible/opacity/rotation/scale) + `BINDABLE_ATTRS_BY_TYPE` (per parser type key) + `bindable_attrs_for()`; `engine/behaviors.py` — `BEHAVIOR_PARAM_SCHEMA` (param → {type: number|value|color|enum, default, values, required}), `BEHAVIOR_DEFAULT_TARGET`, `TRIGGER_KINDS`. Verified by test_c3_new_behavior_appears_without_editor_change: injecting a schema row surfaces its param field in the form with zero editor change.

CXC-BE-SOURCE.title: Live, Bidirectional YAML — A Synced Projection
CXC-BE-SOURCE.status: operational (2026-07-07) — the pop-out hosts a second SourcePanel over the same document; both projections stay in lockstep through the document bus (verified: edit in pop-out → docked view follows).

properties.role: A fourth WC tab, **Source**, showing the current design's `.compose.yaml` as a live view of the `CompositeDocument`. The document/visual stays the source of truth (DP-CXC-2); the YAML is a synced projection (DP-CXC-7 round-trip).
properties.pop-out: a control opens Source in a full-width own window, reusing the Bus-Monitor pop-out mechanism (the WC's 1/3 width is too narrow for comfortable editing).
properties.reuse: the `CompositeDocument` already serializes byte-identical (save→load→save, proven M4) — Source is a view + re-parse + selection link, not a new editor/serializer.
properties.bus-native: an Intelligence editing the design over the document bus updates Source identically to a human — the credo, made visible (watch the YAML change as either drives the canvas).
properties.test: edit a value in Source → canvas updates; select a widget → Source scrolls to it; type an invalid line → error shown, visual state unchanged; pop-out opens full-width and stays synced.
properties.implemented: `composer/source_panel.py` (SourcePanel — engine-native multi-line editor: gutter/line numbers, YAML key tint, cursor + click-to-position + keyboard, block-highlight, error line + status bar) + core handler `composer/source/replace` (whole-document re-parse; commit ONLY on valid parse, `composer/source/status` reports ok/error+line to the bus so an Intelligence sees edit safety too). Buffer sync preserves the user's exact text when it parses to the SAME document (no normalization jump under the cursor); external edits re-project. Selection linkage handles both safe_dump styles (block AND one-line flow mappings). `composer/source/replace` is MQTT-imported — a remote Intelligence document-replace passes the smoke.
properties.change: "Pop-out is the full-width engine DialogWidget overlay — the Bus-Monitor pop-out's in-window mechanism — not a subprocess OS window."
context_for_change: prior_state: "The Bus-Monitor pop-out has two tiers: DialogWidget overlay, or a subprocess OS window when MQTT bridges the buses."

reasoning: "The subprocess tier works for the Bus Monitor because bus traffic IS its content; a subprocess Source editor would need the whole document replicated + edited over the wire — a second document authority, violating DP-CXC-2. The overlay gives the full window width (1380px panel, 0-px identical across platforms) with the document staying in-process."
invalidating_assumption: "That full-WIDTH in-window is enough editing room; a true second-monitor workflow would need the document protocol extended over MQTT first."
properties.status: operational (2026-07-07) — the pop-out hosts a second SourcePanel over the same document; both projections stay in lockstep through the document bus (verified: edit in pop-out → docked view follows).

CXC-BE-RAWSPEC.title: Both Surfaces Edit the Raw Spec, Never the Parsed Tree

properties.constraint: bindings/behaviors/variables are extracted **destructively** at parse (per [SPEC:CXC-BIND] — extraction runs before widget construction). Therefore the binding editor and the Source tab MUST edit the `CompositeDocument`'s **raw spec dicts** and rebuild the canvas from raw spec — they must NEVER re-serialize from the parsed widget tree (the parsed tree has already lost the binding/variable/behavior structure). M4's document model already edits raw dicts; keep that invariant.
properties.test: round-trip a design with bindings + variables + behaviors through the editor → the exported YAML preserves them exactly (no lossy re-serialization).
properties.implemented: three fidelity gaps FOUND AND CLOSED during the build — (1) `LayerDef.from_spec` coerced a non-bool `visible:` (bare-namespace string or binding object) to `True` and DROPPED the raw form: it now stays raw in `properties`, and the Layers-tab eye no longer clobbers a visible binding on export (the binding is the runtime authority; the eye is design-time only); (2) document-level `variables:` (and any unknown top-level key, e.g. `components:`) were dropped by `from_dict`: now a raw `extras` passthrough; (3) the WW preview parsed the stack spec WITHOUT `$var` substitution: it now runs `substitute_variables` exactly as the deployed parse does. Verified: `_REACTIVE_DOC` (bare-string visible, object rotation binding, literal color map, `$alert_period` behavior param, `is_exact` trigger, doc-level variables) round-trips byte-identical (test_c7_*).

properties.rotated-selection: hit-testing of transformed widgets uses the axis-aligned arranged rect (documented [SPEC:CXC-BIND] limitation) — a rotated widget selects by its upright bounds. Acceptable for the indicator tier; the canvas should hint it (e.g. show the AABB on select) rather than pretend the rotated shape is the hit target.
properties.when-canonicalization: trigger matching is canonical — `on`/`true`/`yes`/`1` ≡ on (aligned to the binary state engine). The trigger editor should surface this, and offer the `is_exact:` escape hatch when a user binds a non-binary string state whose values could collide.
properties.implemented: (1) selecting a rotated widget draws the solid AABB + a FAINT outline at the widget's LIVE rotation (read from the preview, so a behavior-driven sweep shows its true orientation) + caption "rotated N° — selects by upright bounds"; the Bindings tab adds the same note when rotation is bound/behaved. (2) The `is:` field carries the canonical-match caption ("on = true = yes = 1"); `is_exact` is a first-class trigger chip — **engine addition**: `Trigger` kind `is_exact` (raw-string compare, no canonicalization), the escape hatch the [SPEC:CXC-BIND] change record pre-sanctioned. (3) Arithmetic detection (`looks_like_expression`: templates, `${…}`, leading `=`, spaced infix operators — URI slashes and hex colors excluded) refuses the edit, keeps the attribute unbound, and logs `{need, context, widget, attr}` to `~/.composeio/dsl_candidates.jsonl` via `composer/dsl/candidate` (bus event, MQTT-imported — an Intelligence can log needs too); an explicit "Need arithmetic? Log it" button captures unprompted needs.

CXC-FL-INTENT.title: Make the Bus Wiring Visible and Listenable
CXC-FL-INTENT.status: operational (2026-07-07) — C1–C9 all PASS (31 compliance tests in `tests/render/test_flow_mode.py`; suites 307 macOS / 303+4skip RPi5); live MQTT smoke 13/13 from BOTH platforms (`tests/render/smoke_flow_discovery_mqtt.py` — a genuinely separate ComposeApp peer on mqtt-broker.local); 11-step walkthrough screenshots macOS↔RPi5 (`tests/render/drive_flow.py` → captures/flow/, 12–24 px/shot Δ≤3, all in the known stroked-circle AA class; the exported artifact byte-identical).

properties.definition: A node-graph view of the design's bus topology, on a Layout↔Flow toggle in the Widget Workshop. It is a *synced projection* of the same `.compose.yaml` as Layout/Bindings/Source (DP-CXC-2/7) — edit in any, all stay in lockstep; not a new authority.
properties.key-insight: ComposeIO is already a graph — namespaces are channels, widgets publish/subscribe. The node view is its honest representation, and it is the natural home for *bus discovery*: choosing what a widget listens for out of open, indeterminate traffic.
properties.status: operational (2026-07-07) — C1–C9 all PASS (31 compliance tests in `tests/render/test_flow_mode.py`; suites 307 macOS / 303+4skip RPi5); live MQTT smoke 13/13 from BOTH platforms (`tests/render/smoke_flow_discovery_mqtt.py` — a genuinely separate ComposeApp peer on mqtt-broker.local); 11-step walkthrough screenshots macOS↔RPi5 (`tests/render/drive_flow.py` → captures/flow/, 12–24 px/shot Δ≤3, all in the known stroked-circle AA class; the exported artifact byte-identical).
properties.implemented: `composer/flowpanel.py` (FlowPane = Bus·Live rail + node graph, ONE interactive widget; FlowInspectorPanel = the WC **Flow** tab; `build_graph(core)` = the pure raw-spec→graph projection) + `composer/discovery.py` (BusDiscovery, the live registry) + the Layout|Flow topbar toggle. Lens + selected connection are BUS STATE (`composer/ww/mode` enum, `composer/flow/selected` json — both MQTT-imported); the WC is now 6 tabs (…/Flow).

properties.definition: Nodes are (a) **widgets** with attribute ports, (b) **namespaces** rendered as fan-in/fan-out hub nodes, and (c) **behaviors** (optional, as nodes on a widget). Wires are bindings/subscriptions. Data flows **publisher widget → namespace node → subscriber widget's attribute**.
properties.rationale: a namespace hub honestly models the bus — one namespace can have many publishers and many subscribers, which a direct widget-to-widget wire cannot express, and it hides nothing (the bus decoupling is the point). "Wire an attribute to a variable" = drag from the attribute port to a namespace node; the wire IS the binding.
properties.sync: the graph reads/writes the CompositeDocument's RAW spec (per [CXC-BE-RAWSPEC]) — never re-serialize from the parsed tree.
properties.test: a design's bindings render as widget↔namespace wires; dragging a new wire writes the binding into the `.compose.yaml`; the Layout/Bindings/Source views reflect it.
properties.implemented: `build_graph(core)` derives nodes/wires ONLY from `doc.bindings()` + declared namespaces (discovery decorates liveness) — so Intelligence-authored and UI-authored wiring are the identical graph by construction (C9 test asserts node/wire-set equality AND byte-equal YAML). FlowNode.kind ∈ namespace|widget|logic — the [CXC-FL-HEADLESS] hook is structural, a widget node carries only id/type/ports. Behaviors render as `» behavior` ports on the widget node (option (c) folded in, not separate nodes — one node per widget keeps the graph legible at this scale). Drag-to-wire: rail-row → widget node (the node EXPANDS to show all bindable ports mid-drag, so the drop picks the exact attribute — ports come from `bindable_attrs_for()`, zero hardcoding) → emits the simplest [SPEC:CXC-BIND] form via `composer/config/widget_changed`; rail-row → open canvas = declare/subscribe only.
properties.change: "Flow's rail + graph are ONE engine widget (FlowPane), not two panels."
context_for_change: prior_state: "[SPEC:CXC-BINDEDIT] deferred drag-connect because a cross-panel drag needs an engine drag/ghost-wire primitive (escalation boundary)."

reasoning: "Making the rail a REGION of the Flow widget keeps every drag pointer-down→pan→release inside one widget's existing gesture surface — drag-to-wire ships without new engine mechanics, and the previs's layout (rail flush against the canvas) is what the design wanted anyway."
invalidating_assumption: "That rail→WC drags (e.g. rail row → Bindings tab) never become necessary; those would still need the cross-panel primitive."
properties.fix-found: `composer/core._h_widget_changed` coerced a BARE-STRING `visible` binding (the sanctioned simplest form) to the Layers-eye bool — the binding was silently dropped on the command path (raw-spec loads were unaffected, which is why BINDEDIT's round-trip tests missed it). Now only bools + the bool vocabulary drive the eye; other strings stay RAW ([CXC-BE-RAWSPEC]).

CXC-FL-DISCOVERY.title: Listen for Indeterminate External Traffic
CXC-FL-DISCOVERY.status: operational (2026-07-07) — MQTT smoke: an undeclared namespace from a separate ComposeApp peer appears live with engine+value; declare-expected flips to subscribed-external on first publish (C7 test drives the previewed widget with it).

properties.definition: a **Bus·Live rail** shows namespaces observed *live on the ComposeBus* (fed by bus monitoring), INCLUDING traffic this design never declared — e.g. an ESP32 emitting `jumpdrive/readiness`. Each entry shows its namespace, state engine, last value, and a live pulse.
properties.test: an external namespace published by another bus participant appears in the rail within one poll; dragging it wires a subscription; a declare-expected binding to a not-yet-live namespace activates when it first publishes.
properties.implemented: `composer/discovery.py` BusDiscovery over the design/external bus — `subscribe_pattern("*", …)` (state + later namespaces) + `bus.on_message` (event liveness, publisher source) + `_bus/discovery` harvest. Registry rows: engine/value/first_seen/last_seen/count/source/app_id; kinds computed against the document (declared-internal / subscribed-external / **expected** (declared, never observed) / live-available); tool plumbing (`_bus/*`, `_app/*`, `composer/*`) excluded. Binding-model addition landed: **`NamespaceDef.external: bool`** — serialized as an additive `external: true` (omitted when False, so pre-FLOW documents round-trip byte-identically); wire-authoring sets it when the namespace is live-but-undeclared or a pattern. The Bindings-tab picker gained a **LIVE ON THE BUS** chip group (same registry), and its `_ensure_declared` now declares external + the observed engine. Both authoring acts real: drag (discover-and-wire, incl. drop-on-open-canvas = subscribe only) and the rail's **"+ listen for (typed name)"** affordance when the filter text names something not live (declare-expected).
properties.status: operational (2026-07-07) — MQTT smoke: an undeclared namespace from a separate ComposeApp peer appears live with engine+value; declare-expected flips to subscribed-external on first publish (C7 test drives the previewed widget with it).

CXC-FL-FILTER.title: Filter the Firehose (P0 — load-bearing, not polish)

properties.definition: over time the bus carries a LOT of namespaces; without filtering, discovery is unusable and widgets are effectively deaf. Filtering has several axes, all standard:
properties.priority: P0. This is the difference between discovery working with 5 namespaces and with 500.
properties.test: with 60+ live namespaces, a `jumpdrive/*` filter narrows the rail to the matching set; a keyword search matches substrings; the count reflects the filter.
properties.implemented: `BusDiscovery.filter(text=, category=)` — substring, trailing-glob (bus `pattern_matches` semantics), fnmatch for other `*` forms; categories all/external/internal/active(≤10s)/live/wired + engine-type names. Rail UI: search LiveInput + chip row (**All** + up to 3 prefix chips COMPUTED from live traffic (`prefix_chips()` — hierarchical namespaces give grouping for free) + external/active/in-design) + the **"showing N of M"** line. C5-tested at 62 namespaces: `jumpdrive/*` → 3 of 62.

CXC-FL-PATTERN.title: A Pattern Is Both a Filter and a Subscription
CXC-FL-PATTERN.status: operational (2026-07-07) — C8 verified at bus, engine (incl. a family member created AFTER wiring), preview, and real-MQTT tiers; family attr-bindings are last-writer-wins across members (documented).

properties.key-insight: the glob you type to *discover* (`jumpdrive/*`) is also an expression a widget can *bind to* — listen to a whole **family** of signals, not one namespace. One language serves discovery (UI) and subscription (runtime): a BusMonitor of all `alert/*`, a tile reacting to any `jumpdrive/*` change, a dradis consuming every `dradis/contact/*`.
properties.test: a widget bound to a pattern receives updates from every matching namespace, including ones that appear after the binding is authored.
properties.change: "NEW BUS PRIMITIVE (ESCALATED, **RATIFIED by David 2026-07-07**): `ComposeIOBus.subscribe_pattern(pattern, cb)` — trailing-glob-only wildcard state subscription, with a transport hook (`Transport.subscribe_pattern`, default no-op; MQTT maps to its native `#` wildcard). Full transport-abstraction (in-process / MQTT / CAN) + the CAN hardware-acceptance-mask model is specified in **[SPEC:CXC-PATSUB]** (`21-composebus-pattern-subscription.lts`)."
context_for_change: prior_state: "The bus had ONLY exact-name subscription; the MQTT transport subscribed `composeio/+/{ns}` per known namespace (plus `_bus/#`), so traffic for a namespace this process never registered NEVER ARRIVED — discovery (C4) and family subscription (C8) were impossible without a bus addition. The kickoff marked this ESCALATE-don't-guess."

reasoning: "Built the MINIMAL primitive whose semantics the bus already implies rather than inventing new ones: `prefix/*` = the prefix and its whole subtree, `*` = everything — exactly MQTT's `#` semantics, so `jumpdrive/*` maps 1:1 to topic filter `composeio/+/jumpdrive/#` and matches the hierarchical-namespace design intent. Delivery = the plain subscribe callback signature with the ACTUAL member namespace passed; fires on every matching publish (liveness, old may equal new — discovery needs the pulse, and re-applying a binding is idempotent). Mid-pattern wildcards (`a/*/b`) raise ValueError — deliberately NOT bus semantics; extending them is a spec change, not a convenience."

rejected_alternative: "Discovery via `_bus/discovery` announcements only (no wildcard) — rejected: it hears only well-behaved ComposeApp peers, not arbitrary/legacy traffic, and cannot carry last values or satisfy C8 at all."

invalidating_assumption: "That trailing-glob covers the real use-cases (family = subtree). If per-level selection (`ship/+/temp`) is ever needed, that is a NEW escalation. Also assumes wildcard MQTT reception at Composer scale is affordable; on very busy brokers a scoped default filter may be needed."

implication: "Semantics note: `p/*` also matches `p` itself (MQTT-`#`-aligned). A declared pattern 'namespace' is NOT registered as a literal namespace anywhere (runtime + Composer both skip it); it exists only as a subscription/declaration. `unsubscribe_pattern` removes the callback; the transport-level wildcard persists (harmless surplus, deduped)."
properties.implemented: bus (`bus.py`: `is_pattern`/`pattern_matches`/`validate_pattern`, `_pattern_subs` notified on local publishes AND transport arrivals) · MQTT (`transport_mqtt.py`: `_pattern_topic` + reconnect re-subscribe; `ComposeApp._add_transport` re-widens late transports) · runtime (`engine/runtime.py`: widget `namespace:`, attr bindings, and behavior triggers all pattern-wire) · WW preview (`composer/chrome.py`: identical wiring on the design bus) · authoring (a `namespaces:` entry may BE a pattern, `external: true`, e.g. the exported `namespace: jumpdrive/*` bus_monitor).
properties.status: operational (2026-07-07) — C8 verified at bus, engine (incl. a family member created AFTER wiring), preview, and real-MQTT tiers; family attr-bindings are last-writer-wins across members (documented).

CXC-FL-ENGINE.title: State-Engine Awareness Makes Indeterminate Signals Legible

properties.role: to interpret an unknown external signal you must know its shape. A discovered namespace surfaces its **state engine** (binary / tri_level / continuous_0_255 / enum / json), and the value-map editor ([CXC-BIND-C8]) translates its values into what the widget uses (`cold/charging/spooled` → gauge value + color). Without the engine an arbitrary message is noise.
properties.implemented: engine resolution priority **declared > peer > inferred** — the design's own NamespaceDef; the peer's `_bus/discovery` announcement (via the NEW additive `engines:` field in `ComposeApp._publish_discovery`); else inferred from observed values with an honest `~` prefix (`~binary`/`~continuous_0_255`/`~json`/`~string`). Shown in the rail row, hub node subtitle, Inspector, and `bus_live` snapshot. Wire-authoring declares the discovered engine, so the value-map editor gets the right vocabulary. Known limit: a raw (non-ComposeApp) publisher with string states reads `~string` until a human/Intelligence sets the engine on the declaration.

properties.items: auto-layout, grouping by module, a minimap, filter-driven focus (show only one namespace's connections). The right-pane **Inspector** shows the selected connection — source namespace, engine, first-seen, and its `when`/`map`/`default` — i.e. exactly "what am I listening for."
properties.deferred: minimap, module grouping, filter-driven graph focus (dim non-matching), persistent node positions — revisit when a real design outgrows two columns.
